title: Impact of Minimum Drinking Age on Alcohol Consumption

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) at the minimum legal drinking age (MLDA) threshold.
- Why: Treatment (legal access to alcohol) turns on deterministically at age 21. With data tightly around the cutoff and a running variable (age in months), RDD identifies the local average causal effect at the threshold.
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff: in absence of treatment, expected alcohol consumption would evolve smoothly through the 21st birthday.
  - No precise manipulation of the running variable at the cutoff: individuals cannot sort just above/below the 21 threshold in a way that correlates with potential outcomes.
- Implementation details:
  - Cutoff is at running_var = 0.5 (based on the treated indicator switching around this point).
  - Local linear regression with triangular kernel on each side of the cutoff.
  - Robustness checks: multiple bandwidths, donut RDD (exclude observations extremely close to cutoff), placebo cutoffs, density (McCrary) test, and a difference-in-means within a very tight window.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code

# 0) Setup -------------------------------------------------------------------
needed <- c("sandwich","lmtest","rdrobust","rddensity")
to_install <- needed[!sapply(needed, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(to_install) > 0) {
  install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1) Read data ---------------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s95_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(path)

# Inspect basic structure
n_total <- nrow(df)
cat("Observations:", n_total, "\n")

# 2) Define cutoff and checks ------------------------------------------------
cutoff <- 0.5
df$x_c <- df$running_var - cutoff
df$treat_from_x <- as.integer(df$running_var >= cutoff)
mismatch <- mean(df$treat_from_x != df$treated)
cat("Share of treatment status mismatches vs. running_var cutoff rule:", round(mismatch, 4), "\n")

# 3) Helper: Local linear RDD with triangular kernel -------------------------
llr_est <- function(y, x, c = 0.5, h = 0.2, donut = 0) {
  xc <- x - c
  idx <- (abs(xc) <= h) & (abs(xc) > donut)
  if (sum(idx) < 20) stop("Not enough observations in the chosen bandwidth.")
  sub <- data.frame(
    y  = y[idx],
    xc = xc[idx],
    D  = as.integer(x[idx] >= c)
  )
  # Triangular kernel weights
  sub$w <- 1 - abs(sub$xc)/h
  sub$w[sub$w < 0] <- 0

  fit <- lm(y ~ D + xc + D:xc, data = sub, weights = w)
  vc  <- sandwich::vcovHC(fit, type = "HC1")
  est <- coef(fit)["D"]
  se  <- sqrt(vc["D", "D"])
  n   <- nrow(sub)
  list(tau = as.numeric(est), se = as.numeric(se), n = n, h = h, donut = donut)
}

print_llr <- function(res, label = "Estimate") {
  ci_l <- res$tau - 1.96 * res$se
  ci_u <- res$tau + 1.96 * res$se
  cat(sprintf("%s (h=%.3f, donut=%.3f): tau = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], N = %d\n",
              label, res$h, res$donut, res$tau, res$se, ci_l, ci_u, res$n))
}

# 4) Main RDD estimate (local linear) ----------------------------------------
set.seed(123)
main_h <- 0.20
main_res <- llr_est(df$y, df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = main_h)
print_llr(main_res, "Main RDD (local linear, triangular)")

# 5) Robustness: alternative bandwidths --------------------------------------
for (h in c(0.10, 0.15, 0.25, 0.30)) {
  res <- llr_est(df$y, df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = h)
  print_llr(res, paste0("Alt BW RDD"))
}

# 6) Robustness: donut RDD (exclude very near cutoff) ------------------------
donut_res <- llr_est(df$y, df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = main_h, donut = 0.02)
print_llr(donut_res, "Donut RDD")

# 7) Robustness: near_cutoff subsample ---------------------------------------
if ("near_cutoff" %in% names(df)) {
  df_near <- subset(df, near_cutoff == 1)
  if (nrow(df_near) >= 30) {
    near_res <- llr_est(df_near$y, df_near$running_var, c = cutoff, h = 0.25)
    print_llr(near_res, "Near-cutoff subsample RDD")
  }
}

# 8) Very tight window: difference-in-means ----------------------------------
tight_h <- 0.05
idx_tight <- abs(df$x_c) <= tight_h
D_tight <- as.integer(df$running_var[idx_tight] >= cutoff)
y_tight <- df$y[idx_tight]
diff_means <- mean(y_tight[D_tight == 1]) - mean(y_tight[D_tight == 0])
cat(sprintf("Tight window (|x|<=%.2f) difference-in-means: %.4f, N=%d\n",
            tight_h, diff_means, sum(idx_tight)))

# 9) Placebo cutoffs ----------------------------------------------------------
placebo_cutoffs <- c(0.30, 0.70)
for (pc in placebo_cutoffs) {
  res <- llr_est(df$y, df$running_var, c = pc, h = 0.20)
  print_llr(res, paste0("Placebo cutoff at ", pc))
}

# 10) rdrobust and density (McCrary) tests -----------------------------------
# Note: we also show standard RDD tools' outputs for reference
if (requireNamespace("rdrobust", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cat("\nrdrobust output (reference):\n")
  rdout <- rdrobust::rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, kernel = "triangular")
  print(rdout)
}
if (requireNamespace("rddensity", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cat("\nMcCrary density test at cutoff (rddensity):\n")
  dens <- rddensity::rddensity(X = df$running_var, c = cutoff)
  print(summary(dens))
}

# 11) Clear numerical result -------------------------------------------------
cat("\nCLEAR RESULT: Estimated jump in alcohol consumption at age 21 (local linear RDD, h=0.20)\n")
cat(sprintf("Tau = %.4f (SE = %.4f), 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], N = %d\n",
            main_res$tau, main_res$se, main_res$tau - 1.96*main_res$se,
            main_res$tau + 1.96*main_res$se, main_res$n))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Reaching the legal drinking age should increase alcohol consumption due to legal access and reduced purchase frictions.
- Magnitude: Moderate local jump. If y is standardized (as the preview suggests), expect a discontinuity around 0.2 to 0.4 standard deviations. If y is in natural units (e.g., drinks/week), a plausible increase is 10–30% relative to the local mean just below 21.
- Interpretation: The estimate is a local average causal effect at the 21st birthday; robustness checks (similar estimates across bandwidths, no density manipulation, and null effects at placebo cutoffs) would support validity.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The identification strategy leverages the age-21 drinking age cutoff as a natural experiment.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Reaching the age of 21 leads to an increase in alcohol consumption.
